title: Sections of smooth algebras modulo an ideal lift over an etale neighbourhood
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $J\subseteq A$ an ideal, $\pi:A\to A/J$ the quotient map, $B$ an $A$-algebra with $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and $\sigma:B\to A/J$ a homomorphism of $A$-algebras. Then there are a ring map $A\to A'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] such that the induced map $\alpha:A/J\to A'/JA'$ is an isomorphism, and a homomorphism of $A$-algebras $\tilde\sigma:B\to A'$ lifting $\sigma$: $q\circ\tilde\sigma=\alpha\circ\sigma$, where $q:A'\to A'/JA'$ is the quotient map.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07M7 (lemma-lift-section-smooth-morphism, line 2139) and its proof (Algebra lemma-application-NL-smooth, lemma-lift-projective-module, lemma-symmetric-algebra-smooth, Algebra lemma-exact-sequence-NL, lemma-NAK, ...); 'smooth A-algebra' there is a smooth ring map, equivalently Spec B -> Spec A smooth (Morphisms, Lemma 01V6, lemma-smooth-characterize)

proof.text: *Reduction to smooth ring maps.* By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] if and only if $A\to B$ is a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]: $B$ is a finitely presented $A$-algebra, $H_1(L_{B/A})=0$ and $\Omega_{B/A}$ is a finite projective $B$-module. So it suffices to prove the following claim $(\ast)$ for every commutative ring $A$, ideal $J\subseteq A$, smooth ring map $A\to B$ and homomorphism of $A$-algebras $\sigma:B\to A/J$: there are a ring map $A\to A'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ etale such that $\alpha:A/J\to A'/JA'$ is an isomorphism, and an $A$-algebra map $\tilde\sigma:B\to A'$ with $q\circ\tilde\sigma=\alpha\circ\sigma$. Throughout, put $N=\ker\sigma\subseteq B$. Since $\sigma$ is a homomorphism of $A$-algebras and $A\to A/J$ is surjective, $\sigma$ is surjective and induces an isomorphism of $A$-algebras $\bar\sigma:B/N\to A/J$; and $JB\subseteq N$ (as $\sigma(j\cdot1)=\pi(j)=0$). Through $\bar\sigma$, every $B/N$-module is an $A/J$-module.

source.place: Lemma 07M7 (lemma-lift-section-smooth-morphism, line 2139): 'B is a smooth A-algebra' is a smooth ring map; first sentence of the proof ('Let J be the kernel of B -> A/I so that B/J = A/I')

proof.text: *The conormal module $N/(N^2+JB)$.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-conormal-sequence-exact] to the smooth ring map $A\to B$, the surjection $\pi:A\to A/J$ and $\beta=\sigma$: the sequence of $A/J$-modules $0\to J/J^2\xrightarrow{u}N/N^2\xrightarrow{v}\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_BB/N\to0$ is exact, $u$ induced by $A\to B$ and $v(b\bmod N^2)=\mathrm db\otimes1$. The image of $u$ is $(J\cdot1+N^2)/N^2$, and $J\cdot1+N^2=JB+N^2$: for $b\in B$ and $j\in J$ choose $a\in A$ with $\sigma(b)=\pi(a)$; then $b-a\cdot1\in N$ and $j\cdot1\in N$, so $bj-aj\cdot1=(b-a\cdot1)(j\cdot1)\in N^2$. Hence $v$ induces an isomorphism of $A/J$-modules $$\overline P:=N/(N^2+JB)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_BB/N,\qquad f\bmod(N^2+JB)\mapsto\mathrm df\otimes1.$$ Since $\Omega_{B/A}$ is a direct summand of a finite free $B$-module [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], $\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_BB/N$ is a direct summand of a finite free $B/N$-module; so $\overline P$ is a finite projective $A/J$-module.

source.place: Lemma 07M7, proof, first paragraph: 'By Algebra, Lemma 06A9 the sequence 0 -> I/I^2 -> J/J^2 -> Omega_{B/A} (x)_B B/J -> 0 is split exact. Thus P-bar = J/(J^2 + IB) = Omega_{B/A} (x)_B B/J is a finite projective A/I-module.' (the identification of the image of I/I^2 with (IB + J^2)/J^2 written out by the agent)

proof.text: *The free case: choice of $f_1,\dots,f_n$ and the ring $C$.* Assume in this and the next three steps the extra hypothesis (F): $\overline P=N/(N^2+JB)$ is a free $A/J$-module with a basis of $n$ elements. Choose $f_1,\dots,f_n\in N$ whose classes form a basis of $\overline P$, let $\mathfrak f=(f_1,\dots,f_n)\subseteq B$ and $C=B/\mathfrak f$, an $A$-algebra via $A\to B\to C$. $C$ is a finitely presented $A$-algebra: if $B\cong A[x_1,\dots,x_m]/(g_1,\dots,g_k)$ and $F_i\in A[x_1,\dots,x_m]$ lift $f_i$, then $C\cong A[x_1,\dots,x_m]/(g_1,\dots,g_k,F_1,\dots,F_n)$. Since $\mathfrak f\subseteq N$, $\sigma$ factors as $B\to C\xrightarrow{\tau}A/J$, $\tau$ a surjective homomorphism of $A$-algebras with $\ker\tau=NC=N/\mathfrak f$. By step 2, the elements $\mathrm df_i\otimes1$ ($i=1,\dots,n$) form a basis of the $B/N$-module $\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_BB/N$.

source.place: Lemma 07M7, proof, second paragraph: 'choose f_1, ..., f_n in J which map to a basis of J/(J^2 + IB). Consider the finitely presented A-algebra C = B/(f_1, ..., f_n)'

proof.text: *The free case: the Jacobi-Zariski sequence of $C$.* Since $A\to B$ is smooth, $H_1(L_{B/A})=0$ and $\Omega_{B/A}$ is (finite) projective [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], so [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-quotient-smooth] applied to $A\to B$ and $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak f$ gives an exact sequence of $C$-modules $$0\to H_1(L_{C/A})\to\mathfrak f/\mathfrak f^2\xrightarrow{\ \delta\ }C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}\xrightarrow{\ w\ }\Omega_{C/A}\to0,\qquad\delta(f_i\bmod\mathfrak f^2)=1\otimes\mathrm df_i.$$ Localization is exact, so for every prime $\bar{\mathfrak q}$ of $C$ the localized sequence is exact, and $H_1(L_{C/A})_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}=\ker\delta_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$, $(\Omega_{C/A})_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}=\operatorname{coker}\delta_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$.

source.place: Lemma 07M7, proof, second paragraph: 'Note that we have an exact sequence 0 -> H_1(L_{C/A}) -> (f_1, ..., f_n)/(f_1, ..., f_n)^2 -> Omega_{B/A} (x)_B C -> Omega_{C/A} -> 0 see Algebra, Lemma 00S2 (note that H_1(L_{B/A}) = 0 and that Omega_{B/A} is finite projective, in particular flat so the Tor group vanishes)'

proof.text: *The free case: $\delta$ is an isomorphism at every prime containing $NC$.* Let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be a prime with $N\subseteq\mathfrak q$ (so $\mathfrak f\subseteq\mathfrak q$) and $\bar{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak q/\mathfrak f$ the corresponding prime of $C$; these $\bar{\mathfrak q}$ are exactly the primes of $C$ containing $NC$. (a) *Rank.* As $\Omega_{B/A}$ is finite projective, $(\Omega_{B/A})_{\mathfrak q}$ is a finite free $B_{\mathfrak q}$-module, of some rank $r$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-rank-locally-constant]. With $\kappa=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, $\dim_\kappa\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B\kappa=r$; but $B\to\kappa$ factors through $B/N$ (as $N\subseteq\mathfrak q$), so $\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B\kappa=(\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_BB/N)\otimes_{B/N}\kappa$ is free over $\kappa$ with basis the images of $\mathrm df_1,\dots,\mathrm df_n$ (step 3). Hence $r=n$. (b) *Surjectivity.* $(C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A})_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}=(\Omega_{B/A})_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak f(\Omega_{B/A})_{\mathfrak q}$ is a free $C_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$-module of rank $n$, finitely generated over the local ring $C_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$ with residue field $\kappa$, and modulo the maximal ideal it is $\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B\kappa$, spanned by the images of $1\otimes\mathrm df_i=\delta(f_i)$. By Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] the elements $\delta(f_i)$ generate $(C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A})_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$, i.e. $\delta_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$ is surjective. (c) *Injectivity.* Let $\psi:C_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}^{\oplus n}\to(\mathfrak f/\mathfrak f^2)_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$, $e_i\mapsto f_i$; it is surjective since the $f_i$ generate $\mathfrak f$. Choose an isomorphism $\theta:(C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A})_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}\cong C_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}^{\oplus n}$ (by (b), rank $n$). Then $\theta\circ\delta_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}\circ\psi$ is a surjective endomorphism of the finite $C_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$-module $C_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}^{\oplus n}$, hence an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-surjective-endomorphism-bijective]. So $\psi$ is injective, hence an isomorphism, and $\delta_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}=\theta^{-1}\circ(\theta\delta_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}\psi)\circ\psi^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. By step 4, $H_1(L_{C/A})_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}=0$ and $(\Omega_{C/A})_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}=0$.

source.place: Lemma 07M7, proof, second paragraph: 'For any prime q containing J of B the module Omega_{B/A,q} is free of rank n because Omega_{B/A} is finite projective and because Omega_{B/A} (x)_B B/J is free of rank n (see Algebra, Lemma 00NX). By our choice of f_1, ..., f_n the map ((f)/(f)^2)_q -> Omega_{B/A,q} is surjective modulo J. Hence ... has to be an isomorphism (by Algebra, Lemma 00DV the map is surjective and for example by Algebra, Lemma 05G8 because ((f)/(f)^2)_q is generated by n elements the map is injective). Thus H_1(L_{C/A})_q = 0 and Omega_{C/A,q} = 0.'

proof.text: *The free case: an etale localization $C_h$.* By step 5 and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-near-prime-naive-cotangent-vanishing] (applied to the finitely presented $A$-algebra $C$, step 3), for every prime $\bar{\mathfrak q}$ of $C$ containing $NC$ there is $h'\in C\setminus\bar{\mathfrak q}$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C_{h'}\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-localize-upstairs] (with $B:=C$, $\mathfrak b:=NC$) there is $h\in C$ whose image in $C/NC$ is a unit such that $\operatorname{Spec}C_h\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale. Since $\tau:C\to A/J$ has kernel $NC$, $\tau(h)$ is a unit of $A/J$, so $\tau$ extends to a homomorphism of $A$-algebras $\tau_h:C_h\to A/J$, $c/h^k\mapsto\tau(c)\tau(h)^{-k}$, with kernel $NC_h\supseteq JC_h$.

source.place: Lemma 07M7, proof, second paragraph: 'By Algebra, Lemma 07BU we see that A -> C is smooth at the prime q-bar of C corresponding to q. Since Omega_{C/A,q} = 0 it is actually etale at q-bar. Thus A -> C is etale at all primes of C containing JC. By Lemma 07M0 we can find an f in C mapping to an invertible element of C/JC such that A -> C_f is etale. By our choice of f it is still true that C_f/JC_f = A/I.'

proof.text: *The free case: cutting out $A/J$ by an idempotent, and conclusion.* Put $S=C_h/JC_h$, an $A/J$-algebra via $A\to C_h$; by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-quotient-base-change] (applied to $A\to C_h$ and $J$), $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ is etale. $\tau_h$ induces $s:S\to A/J$, a homomorphism of $A$-algebras, hence of $A/J$-algebras. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-idempotent-splitting] there is an idempotent $e\in S$ with $s(e)=1$ such that $s$ induces an isomorphism of $A/J$-algebras $s_e:S_e\to A/J$. Choose $g\in C_h$ mapping to $e$ and put $A'=(C_h)_g$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lift-invertible-element] (1), applied to the ring $C_h$, the element $g$ and the ideal $(1-g)C_h$ (modulo which $g$ is $1$, a unit), $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}C_h$ is etale; composing with the etale $\operatorname{Spec}C_h\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ (step 6), $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (2). Localization commutes with quotients, so $A'/JA'=(C_h)_g/J(C_h)_g\cong S_e$; let $t:A'/JA'\to A/J$ be this isomorphism followed by $s_e$, an isomorphism of $A$-algebras. Then $t\circ\alpha:A/J\to A/J$ is a homomorphism of $A$-algebras, hence the identity; so $\alpha=t^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. Let $\tilde\sigma:B\to C\to C_h\to A'$ be the composite of the canonical $A$-algebra maps. For $b\in B$, $t(q(\tilde\sigma(b)))=\tau_h(\bar b/1)=\tau(\bar b)=\sigma(b)=t(\alpha(\sigma(b)))$; since $t$ is injective, $q\circ\tilde\sigma=\alpha\circ\sigma$. This proves $(\ast)$ under (F).

source.place: Lemma 07M7, proof, last sentences: 'The map C_f/IC_f -> A/I is surjective and etale by Algebra, Lemma 00U7. Hence A/I is isomorphic to the localization of C_f/IC_f at some element g in C, see Algebra, Lemma 00U8. Set A' = C_{fg} to conclude the proof.' (00U7 and 00U8 are carried by lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-idempotent-splitting; the verification of alpha and of the lift written out by the agent)

proof.text: *The case (H): adding a symmetric algebra.* Assume now hypothesis (H): there are $n\ge0$ and a finite projective $A$-module $Q$ with an isomorphism of $A/J$-modules $\overline P\oplus Q/JQ\cong(A/J)^{\oplus n}$. Let $\operatorname{Sym}_A(Q)$ be the symmetric algebra and $\iota:Q\to\operatorname{Sym}_A(Q)$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. It is the quotient of the tensor algebra by the ideal generated by the $x\otimes y-y\otimes x$, which is homogeneous and lies in degrees $\ge2$; so $\operatorname{Sym}_A(Q)=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}\operatorname{Sym}^d(Q)$ is graded, $\operatorname{Sym}^0=A$, $\iota:Q\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Sym}^1$, and $\operatorname{Sym}^d$ is spanned by products of $d$ elements of $\iota(Q)$. Let $\varepsilon:\operatorname{Sym}_A(Q)\to A$ be the $A$-algebra map with $\varepsilon\circ\iota=0$ (universal property); it is the projection to degree $0$. Put $B'=B\otimes_A\operatorname{Sym}_A(Q)$, $j:B\to B'$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$, and $p=\mathrm{id}_B\otimes\varepsilon:B'\to B$, a $B$-algebra map with $p\circ j=\mathrm{id}_B$. *Smoothness:* $A\to\operatorname{Sym}_A(Q)$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-finite-projective-smooth], so $j:B\to B\otimes_A\operatorname{Sym}_A(Q)$ is smooth (base change) and $A\to B\to B'$ is smooth (composition) [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition]. Put $\sigma'=\sigma\circ p:B'\to A/J$, an $A$-algebra map, and $N'=\ker\sigma'$. *Computation of $N'/(N'^2+JB')$:* as $B$-modules $B'=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}B\otimes_A\operatorname{Sym}^d(Q)$ with degree $0$ part $j(B)$, and $\mathfrak k:=\ker p=\bigoplus_{d\ge1}B\otimes_A\operatorname{Sym}^d(Q)$; so $N'=p^{-1}(N)=j(N)\oplus\mathfrak k$. Then $N'^2=j(N^2)+N\mathfrak k+\mathfrak k^2$ and $JB'=j(JB)\oplus J\mathfrak k$, with $N\mathfrak k,J\mathfrak k,\mathfrak k^2\subseteq\mathfrak k$, so $N'^2+JB'=j(N^2+JB)\oplus(N\mathfrak k+J\mathfrak k+\mathfrak k^2)$ and $N'/(N'^2+JB')\cong N/(N^2+JB)\oplus\mathfrak k/(N\mathfrak k+J\mathfrak k+\mathfrak k^2)$. Since $\mathfrak k^2=\bigoplus_{d\ge2}B\otimes_A\operatorname{Sym}^d(Q)$, $\mathfrak k=(B\otimes_AQ)\oplus\mathfrak k^2$, and modulo $\mathfrak k^2$ the submodule $N\mathfrak k+J\mathfrak k$ is $(N+JB)(B\otimes_AQ)=N(B\otimes_AQ)$ (as $JB\subseteq N$). Hence $\mathfrak k/(N\mathfrak k+J\mathfrak k+\mathfrak k^2)\cong(B/N)\otimes_AQ\cong(A/J)\otimes_AQ=Q/JQ$ via $\bar\sigma$. These are isomorphisms of modules over $B'/N'=B/N\cong A/J$, so $N'/(N'^2+JB')\cong\overline P\oplus Q/JQ\cong(A/J)^{\oplus n}$: $(A\to B',\sigma')$ satisfies (F). By steps 3-7 there are $A\to A'$ etale with $\alpha$ an isomorphism and $\tilde\sigma':B'\to A'$ with $q\circ\tilde\sigma'=\alpha\circ\sigma'$. Then $\tilde\sigma=\tilde\sigma'\circ j$ is an $A$-algebra map and $q\circ\tilde\sigma=\alpha\circ\sigma'\circ j=\alpha\circ\sigma\circ p\circ j=\alpha\circ\sigma$. This proves $(\ast)$ under (H).

source.place: Lemma 07M7, proof, first paragraph: 'Set B' = B (x)_A Sym_A^*(K). Since A -> Sym_A^*(K) is smooth by Lemma 07M6 we see that B -> B' is smooth which in turn implies that A -> B' is smooth (see Algebra, Lemmas 00T4 and 00TC). Moreover the section Sym^*_A(K) -> A determines a section B' -> B ... We have JB' in J' and B (x)_A K in J'. These maps combine to give an isomorphism (A/I)^n = J/(J^2 + IB) (+) K-bar -> J'/((J')^2 + IB'). Thus, after replacing B by B' we may assume that J/(J^2 + IB) is a free A/I-module of rank n.' (the composition is Algebra 00TD; the computation of J'/((J')^2 + IB') written out by the agent)

proof.text: *The general case: lifting a complement over an etale neighbourhood.* Let $A\to B$, $\sigma$ be arbitrary. By step 2, $\overline P$ is finite projective over $A/J$, so there are $n\ge0$ and an $A/J$-module $\overline K$ with $\overline P\oplus\overline K\cong(A/J)^{\oplus n}$; $\overline K$ is finite projective. By [lem-weil-pbc-lift-projective-module-etale] there are a ring map $A\to A_1$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A_1\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ etale and $\alpha_1:A/J\to A_1/JA_1$ an isomorphism, and a finite projective $A_1$-module $Q$ with $Q/JQ\cong\overline K\otimes_{A/J}A_1/JA_1$. Put $B_1=A_1\otimes_AB$, $\iota_1:B\to B_1$, $b\mapsto1\otimes b$; $A_1\to B_1$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] (1). Let $\sigma_1:B_1\to A_1/JA_1$ be the $A_1$-algebra map $a\otimes b\mapsto\bar a\,\alpha_1(\sigma(b))$ (universal property of $\otimes_A$), so $\sigma_1\circ\iota_1=\alpha_1\circ\sigma$, and $N_1=\ker\sigma_1$, $\overline P_1=N_1/(N_1^2+JB_1)$. By step 2 for $(A_1,JA_1,B_1,\sigma_1)$ and [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change], $$\overline P_1\cong\Omega_{B_1/A_1}\otimes_{B_1}B_1/N_1\cong(B_1\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A})\otimes_{B_1}(A_1/JA_1)\cong\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_B(A_1/JA_1)\cong(\Omega_{B/A}\otimes_BB/N)\otimes_{A/J}A_1/JA_1\cong\overline P\otimes_{A/J}A_1/JA_1,$$ where $B$ acts on $A_1/JA_1$ through $\sigma_1\circ\iota_1=\alpha_1\circ\sigma$ (associativity of $\otimes$). Hence $\overline P_1\oplus Q/JQ\cong(\overline P\oplus\overline K)\otimes_{A/J}A_1/JA_1\cong(A_1/JA_1)^{\oplus n}$: $(A_1,JA_1,A_1\to B_1,\sigma_1)$ satisfies (H) (note $(JA_1)B_1=JB_1$).

source.place: Lemma 07M7, proof, first paragraph: 'Choose an integer n and a direct sum decomposition A/I^n = P-bar (+) K-bar. By Lemma 07M5 we can find an etale ring map A -> A' which induces an isomorphism A/I -> A'/IA' and a finite projective A-module K which lifts K-bar. We may and do replace A by A'.' (that the replacement keeps P-bar, by base change of differentials, Algebra Lemma 00RV, written out by the agent)

proof.text: *The general case: conclusion.* By step 8 applied to $(A_1,JA_1,B_1,\sigma_1)$ there are a ring map $A_1\to A'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A_1$ etale and $\beta:A_1/JA_1\to A'/(JA_1)A'=A'/JA'$ an isomorphism, and an $A_1$-algebra map $\tilde\sigma_1:B_1\to A'$ with $q\circ\tilde\sigma_1=\beta\circ\sigma_1$. Then $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is the composite of the etale morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A_1\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, hence etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (2); the map $A/J\to A'/JA'$ induced by $A\to A_1\to A'$ is $\alpha=\beta\circ\alpha_1$, an isomorphism; and $\tilde\sigma=\tilde\sigma_1\circ\iota_1:B\to A'$ is a homomorphism of $A$-algebras with $q\circ\tilde\sigma=\beta\circ\sigma_1\circ\iota_1=\beta\circ\alpha_1\circ\sigma=\alpha\circ\sigma$. This proves $(\ast)$, hence the lemma (step 1).

reviewed.note: Reviewed by the lead (opus-relaunch6). Ten steps along the proof of 07M7, eleven new nodes: a definition node for smooth ring maps via the naive cotangent complex (07BN/00T2; Mathlib leaf Algebra.Smooth, Smooth/Basic.lean:540, with H1Cotangent for H_1(NL)), the identification lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine (01V6+02H6, unsplit; the first node connecting def-sbc-smooth-morphisms with smooth ring maps), and the lemmas of the proof: base change and composition of smooth maps (00T4/00TD; Mathlib leaf, lines 573/568 verified), the conormal sequence 06A9, lifting projective modules along an etale neighbourhood 07M5, Sym of a finite projective module is smooth 07M6, base change of differentials 00RV (leaf, Kaehler/TensorProduct.lean:189), the Jacobi-Zariski sequence 00S2 for a quotient, surjective endomorphisms of finite modules 05G8 (leaf, OrzechProperty.lean:108 with CommRing.orzechProperty), etale near a prime from the vanishing of NL 07BU, and the localization lemma 07M0. The three agent-written parts (survival of the conormal module under A -> A_1 via base change of differentials, the computation for B (x) Sym(K), the final check) read correctly. Step 7's use of lem-weil-pbc-lift-invertible-element for 'Spec (C_h)_g -> Spec C_h is etale' is roundabout (a principal open immersion is etale) but valid.

split_report.summary: Proof written in 10 steps following Stacks 07M7 exactly (reduction to smooth ring maps; conormal module via 06A9; free case: C = B/(f), Jacobi-Zariski sequence, rank/Nakayama/05G8 at primes containing NC, etale at those primes (07BU), 07M0 localization, idempotent splitting (00U7/00U8) and A' = C_{hg}; case (H) via B (x) Sym(Q) (07M6, 00T4, 00TD) with the conormal computation written out; general case via 07M5 and base change of differentials (00RV)). The DAG had no node for smooth ring maps (Stacks 00T2) or for the identification with def-sbc-smooth-morphisms (01V6/02H6): created def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map (Mathlib leaf Algebra.Smooth) and lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine (unsplit). Created 9 further nodes for the cited Stacks lemmas (06A9, 07M5, 07M6, 00T4+00TD, 00RV, 00S2 specialised, 05G8, 07BU+00U1, 07M0); 3 of them Mathlib leaves.
